summary: Squaw Mountain (now Tumala Mountain) lookout, Clackamas County, OR: 1916 frame cabin, staffed into the late 1950s, removed 1966. No source describes remains.

facts.design: 1916 frame cabin; 1930s replacement given as a 12x12 ft cab on a pole platform tower, or an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Deactivated 1964, removed (1966 per two sources). The Outbound says it once stood atop the summit.

staffing.status: last staffing record found: manned 25 days in the 1957 district report

access.note: Hiking route from Twin Springs Trailhead, per The Outbound; no agency page checked for current access

visit.trail_note: About 3.6 miles round trip from Twin Springs Trailhead; the trail meets an old service road near the summit

events.note: Frame cabin, per firetower.org and firelookout.com

New standard lookout house 14 ft square, enclosed in glass (July 31, 1932 report); lightning-safeguard construction reported July 24, 1932
Kenneth Dart worked as lookout man for the summer
Elmer Klutke stationed on Squaw Mountain lookouts during fire season
Manned 25 days (1957 district report, posted February 1958)
Catwalk built, lookout painted, two new shutters installed (1957 district report)
Last half mile of access road improved (entry dated January 15, 1959; 1958 report)
Oregon Lookouts history: deactivated; then marked removed with no date
Removal year per firetower.org and firelookout.com; Oregon Lookouts gives no removal year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org says the 1930s replacement was a 12x12 ft cab on a pole platform tower; firelookout.com says an L-4 cab. Both agree on the 1916 frame cabin. The story reports both readings.
A July 1932 newspaper describes a new 14-foot-square house, which does not match the 12x12 ft cab in firetower.org. The story treats the 1932 house as a separate report.
firetower.org and firelookout.com give 1966 for removal; Oregon Lookouts gives deactivation in 1964 and no removal year. The story gives 1964 for deactivation and 1966 for removal.
A 1918 newspaper gives 4972 ft. firetower.org gives 4,771 ft (1,454 m) and Wikipedia gives 4,773 ft (1,455 m). The brief's 1454.2 m matches the later figures, so it is kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 3.0 not used: the only height in the sources is the 1918 cabin's about 10 feet, not the later tower. Brief access 'unknown' replaced by a public hiking route per The Outbound (user-submitted guide, not an agency); no agency page checked. A Facebook post by Forgotten Oregon appeared in search results suggesting something of the lookout remains; it could not be read, so it is unverified. Check for footings or remains before any visit note. The 2007 rename rests on Wikipedia; verify against GNIS. No new photos recorded.
